title: Adaptive Multi-Split ML Protocol over Constrained WAN Links (Prelude <1.5 GB Client <-> Edge Core)
hypothesis: Dynamically splitting the neural execution graph at low-dimensional cut-layer boundaries L_c in {1, 2, 3, 4} with INT8 boundary activation quantization and QUIC RTT/bandwidth adaptation reduces per-step WAN synchronization latency by >= 55% on a constrained 20 Mbps / 60 ms RTT residential link while keeping client GPU VRAM strictly <= 1536 MiB and gamer preemption <= 412 ms.

invariants_enforced.cohort_isolation: Pre-Ampere (SM < 8.0, FP32) isolated from Ampere+ (SM >= 8.0, BF16)

controls.positive_control: Adaptive Multi-Split ML with INT8 cut-layer quantization and dynamic L_c selection over 20 Mbps / 60 ms RTT WAN link
controls.negative_control: Monolithic full-branch FP32 sync over the same 20 Mbps / 60 ms RTT WAN link without cut-layer splitting
